params.name: created_at.lt
params.description: Include timestamps strictly less than lt. RFC3339 format, like `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.

params.name: created_at.lte
params.description: Include timestamps less than or equal to lte. RFC3339 format, like `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.

params.name: created_at.eq
params.description: Include timestamps exactly equal to eq. RFC3339 format, like `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.

params.name: created_at.gte
params.description: Include timestamps greater than or equal to gte. RFC3339 format, like `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.

params.name: created_at.gt
params.description: Include timestamps strictly greater than gt. RFC3339 format, like `2006-01-02T15:04:05Z`.

params.name: limit
params.description: Number of results to return. Defaults to 100 if no limit is provided.

params.name: type
params.description: Retrieve all (default) or optionally filter by event type.

params.name: is_test
params.description: Filter for test events (true) or real events (false). Defaults to false (real events only).

params.name: order
params.description: Sort order for results by created_at. Defaults to ASC (oldest first).

params.name: page_cursor
params.description: Cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page.

items.docs:
This endpoint enables you to fetch a list of events that have been created by the system.
You can use query parameters to filter the results by the `created_at` time using `created_at.lt`, `created_at.gt`, etc. and you can
`limit` the number of events returned.

Use `page_cursor` from the previous response to paginate through results. Use `order` to control sort direction (ASC or DESC by created_at).
Events returned will be ordered by `created_at` in ascending order by default.

params.name: is_test
params.description: Filter for test events (true) or real events (false). Defaults to false (real events only).

items.docs:
Get an Event by its (event) id, the event must have been created by the system and you must be the owner of the
the event, you can get an event id by either listing events or via a webhook integration.
